newsitem.title: UK: Radius warns on profits, forex impact.
newsitem.headline: Radius warns on profits, forex impact.

text.p: British computer services group Radius Plc warned on Thursday that its pre-tax profit for 1996 would be lower than market expectations due to customer and exchange rate problems.

In a statement issued ahead of its results report due on March 19, the company said it had learned this week that one of its North American retail customers had filed for protection against its creditors.
"Radius is involved with this customer on a high value project which had been completed and accepted, but which has a final substantial stage payment due on April 1, 1997.

"Although the customer is not yet in default, the directors consider it is appropriate to adopt a prudent position and to provide against the outstanding amount as the timing and terms of the settlement cannot be certain," it added.

In addition to this worry, the company said it also had unrealised foreign currency translation losses at the balance sheet date, "which will impact on the results for the year ended 31 December 1996".
Approximately 25 percent of the Group's turnover is denominated in foreign currency.
"The Directors now anticipate that profits before taxation for 1996 will be about 10 percent lower than the comparative level achieved in 1995 (1.8 million stg).

"As a consequence of these non-recurring charges, the reported results for 1996 will not reflect the strong underlying performance of the public sector, professional, engineering and printing divisions.
Radius concluded that its prospects for 1997 were "underpinned by improved order books and a strong cash and balance sheet position".
After the statement, the company's shares were marked down 10 pence to 51-1/2 pence.
